title: Empirical-Grounding Filter at DECIDE (Tier-2 Methodology Vocabulary)
summary: At ADR-drafting time the dyad asks whether the commitment is grounded by PLAY evidence, stakeholder-articulated demand, spike validation, or structural operationalization; when none applies the ADR takes Conditional Acceptance or the adr-deferred- filename pattern.
context: Cycle 019's research named C7: the over-engineering failure mode, where it occurs, traces to research-surveyed possibilities surviving into ADRs without an empirical filter. Loop 6's cross-project investigation showed YAGNI as the dominant pattern when DECIDE applies an empirical filter and kitchen-sink as the localized failure mode when it does not.
commitment: At ADR-drafting time, the practitioner-and-agent dyad applies a felt-trigger asking whether the commitment is empirically grounded by one of four paths: PLAY evidence; stakeholder-articulated demand; spike validation; structural operationalization. When grounded, the ADR proceeds. When not, it takes the Conditional Acceptance annotation or the `adr-deferred-` filename pattern.

warrants.claim: Cross-project evidence (zani, llm-orc, plexus; ~26 ADRs sampled) shows YAGNI when an empirical filter is applied at DECIDE and kitchen-sink when it is not.
The methodology's own evidence base is single-cycle and agent-conducted, which supports vocabulary-level recognition but not heavy structural enforcement.

sub_decisions.title: Target 2: Discriminating criterion
sub_decisions.commitment: The Kitchen-Sink Mechanism versus Kitchen-Sink Outcome distinction is acknowledged as a gap; no discriminating criterion is committed this cycle.
sub_decisions.rationale: The cycle's evidence does not supply a criterion that separates over-engineering from legitimate elaboration without a trivially-passing escape hatch.

sub_decisions.title: Target 3: Standalone at commitment time
sub_decisions.commitment: Two senses of standalone are distinguished: commitment-time (the ADR commits now) and grounding-completion (validation accrues later).
sub_decisions.rationale: Conditional Acceptance is the institutional pattern (llm-orc ADR-016) for committing now and validating on the way; conflating the two senses would either block commitment or hide the pending validation.

rejected_alternatives.title: Hard gate blocking ungrounded ADRs
rejected_alternatives.reason: Would itself instantiate the C7 pattern: heavy structural enforcement from a thin, single-cycle evidence base.

rejected_alternatives.title: No filter; rely on PLAY to pull features back
rejected_alternatives.reason: PLAY operates after BUILD; the kitchen-sink mechanism operates upstream at DECIDE.

graduation_trigger: If two to four cycles record the felt-trigger at ADR-drafting with Conditional Acceptance or adr-deferred- forms in use, the filter becomes a Decide Skill step; if the forms go unused, the vocabulary is retained and the step is not added.

positive: ADRs carry their grounding path explicitly.
negative: The discriminating-criterion gap is acknowledged, not resolved.
neutral: Conditional Acceptance and adr-deferred- are institutional patterns borrowed from llm-orc and plexus.
